items.stem: For steady one-dimensional heat conduction through a plane wall, Fourier's law says the heat-transfer rate is:

options.text: Proportional to the temperature difference and inversely proportional to the wall thickness
options.rationale: Correct: q = kA(dT)/L, rising with dT and falling with thickness.
Conduction is driven by the temperature difference.
Thicker walls reduce, not increase, conduction for a given dT.

options.text: Zero whenever the two surfaces differ in temperature
options.rationale: A temperature difference drives a nonzero conduction rate.

items.explanation: Correct: q = kA(dT)/L, rising with dT and falling with thickness.

items.stem: In a steady-flow control volume with one inlet and one outlet and no heat or work interactions, the first law reduces to a balance in which:

options.text: The energy entering with the inlet stream equals the energy leaving with the outlet stream
options.rationale: Correct: with no heat/work and steady state, energy in equals energy out.

options.text: Energy accumulates without limit in the control volume
Mass is created to balance the energy
options.rationale: Mass is conserved; it is not created.

options.text: The outlet energy is always double the inlet energy
options.rationale: Nothing doubles the energy in this balance.

items.explanation: Correct: with no heat/work and steady state, energy in equals energy out.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the modes of heat transfer are correct?

options.text: Conduction transfers heat through a material without bulk motion of the material
options.rationale: Correct: conduction is diffusion of energy through a medium.

options.text: Radiation can transfer heat across a vacuum
options.rationale: Correct: thermal radiation needs no medium.

options.text: Convection requires no fluid motion at all
Conduction requires a vacuum to occur
options.rationale: Conduction occurs within matter, not in a vacuum.
Radiation occurs for any body above absolute zero, including in vacuum.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: conduction is diffusion of energy through a medium. Correct: thermal radiation needs no medium.
